title: Lowest-Calorie Vegetables

seo.title: Lowest-Calorie Vegetables per 100 Grams
seo.meta_description: Cucumber and lettuce are around 15 calories per 100 g, zucchini about 17, tomato 18, and green bell pepper about 20. Most are over 90% water.
seo.search_intent: Compare very low-calorie vegetables with concrete per-100-gram values.

excerpt: Among common raw vegetables, cucumber and lettuce are near 15 calories per 100 g, zucchini about 17, tomato 18, green bell pepper around 20, and spinach about 23. Their very high water content explains the low energy density.
content_html:
Once vegetables get down into the teens of calories per 100 g, the ranking differences become tiny. Most of these foods are very low in energy because they are mostly water.

Some of the lowest per 100 g

Raw vegetableApprox. kcal/100 g
Cucumber with peel~15
Lettuce~15–17
Zucchini~17
Tomato~18
Green bell pepper~20
Spinach~23

Values are rounded from composition databases such as USDA FoodData Central.

Cooking can change calorie density

Boiling without added fat contributes essentially no new calories, although water gain or loss can change calories per 100 g. Roasting removes water and concentrates the food. Two tablespoons of oil add roughly 240 calories to the dish regardless of whether the vegetable started at 15 or 25 calories per 100 g.

Lower calorie does not automatically mean better

Broccoli, carrots, or peas may contain more calories than cucumber, but they also provide different amounts of fiber, carotenoids, vitamin C, folate, or protein. Energy density is only one dimension.

Serving size matters more than tiny ranking gaps

Two hundred grams of zucchini is around 34 calories and 200 g of tomato around 36. That 2-calorie difference is meaningless in practice. The value of this list is understanding which foods are very low in energy, not chasing first place.

For vegetables, cooking method and added ingredients usually change the final plate more than a few calories between raw varieties.

faq.question: Which vegetable has the fewest calories?
faq.answer: Cucumber and several lettuces are among the lowest common options at roughly 15 calories per 100 g.

faq.question: Is tomato much higher than cucumber?
faq.answer: No. Tomato is around 18 kcal/100 g versus about 15 for cucumber.

faq.question: Does cooking add calories?
faq.answer: Heat itself does not, but oil, butter, sauces, and loss of water can raise calorie density.
